answer: To resist sybils, charge a quadratic identity bond that grows with how many unproven accounts share a sponsor graph, and vest that bond only after N unique challenge attestations from already-established graders. A factory that sprouts a grove of clones quickly faces exploding collateral, while a careful newcomer pays a modest velvet-smooth fee. The bond then sits in an escrow oasis for two epochs; coordinated collapse of the clone set slashes it, so cheap identity floods become unprofitable.
